findings.locator: PDF p2 / printed p1, prose below Fig1
findings.source_claim: Says that moving away from the tangent point makes the approximation grow less accurate.
findings.correction_or_qualification: Describe a local approximation whose error tends to zero suitably near the base point; increasing distance does not universally increase error monotonically.
findings.checked_deduction: For the source own cosine linearization L=1 at0, the error is0 again at2pi and is2 atpi. More locally, f(x)=x^2(x-a)^2 has tangent0 at0, positive error inside(0,a), and zero error again at arbitrarily small a>0.

findings.locator: PDF p3 / printed p2, final sentence of Proof1 and last line of Proof5
findings.source_claim: Writes f(x)=x for f=sin(x), and f(x)=f(0)+fprime(0)x=1+rx for f=(1+x)^r.
findings.correction_or_qualification: Use approximation signs for f, or define the linear Taylor polynomial L and write L(x)=x and L(x)=1+rx.
findings.checked_deduction: sin(x)=x is not an identity on any open interval; sin(1) is not1. For r=2, the exact power is1+2x+x^2, not1+2x. The listed approximations above these lines are correct.

findings.locator: PDF p5 / printed p4, displayed time-dilation expansion immediately below Fig3
findings.correction_or_qualification: Keep T: Tprime approximately T[1+v^2/(2c^2)], or normalize and write Tprime/T approximately1+v^2/(2c^2).
findings.checked_deduction: The printed right side is dimensionless while Tprime is a time interval. Atv=0 it incorrectly gives1 rather thanT. The inverse-square-root expansion itself has the correct positive coefficient.

findings.locator: PDF p5 / printed p4, bracketed explanation to right of the time-dilation expansion
findings.checked_deduction: For an actual fourth power the linear coefficient is4; the intended r=-1/2 produces coefficient-1/2, which with u=-v^2/c^2 gives the required positive half-beta-squared term. The page image confirms a printed4, not merely an extraction error.

findings.locator: PDF p2 general linear formula; p4 inference of fprime(0) and limit; pp5-6 quadratic formula
findings.source_claim: Uses approximate equality to infer exact derivative/limit data and gives a general quadratic formula without remainder conditions.
findings.correction_or_qualification: State f(x0+h)=f(x0)+fprime(x0)h+o(h) for differentiable f. For the quadratic formula, sufficient local C2 regularity gives remainder o(h^2); stronger derivative bounds permit numerical error bounds.
findings.checked_deduction: Only a remainder small compared with h can be divided by h and discarded in a limit. A bare small absolute discrepancy such as an added |h| need not preserve differentiability. All specific elementary functions here are smooth on their stated real domains, so the worked derivative and limit results are correct.

findings.locator: PDF p5 / printed p4, Geometric picture paragraph
findings.source_claim: Calls the Taylor quadratic a best-fit parabola.
findings.correction_or_qualification: Specify the polynomial of degree at most2 matching value, first derivative and second derivative at the base point; this is not an unspecified least-squares fit over an interval.
findings.checked_deduction: The three matching conditions uniquely give a=f(x0), b=fprime(x0), c=fsecond(x0)/2 in powers of h. If fsecond(x0)=0, as for sin at0 in the next list, the polynomial is linear rather than a nondegenerate parabola.

findings.locator: PDF pp2-7, basic approximation lists, Examples2/5 and Planet Quirk
findings.source_claim: Lists logarithmic, real-power, trigonometric and relativistic approximations with only a near-zero cue.
findings.correction_or_qualification: Use radians for trigonometric inputs; require1+x>0 for the logarithm, arbitrary real powers and the reciprocal-square-root examples; hold r fixed. Require|v|<c for the real gamma factor and |v|/c much less than1 for its truncation.
findings.checked_deduction: Derivative formulas supply the stated coefficients on these domains. Smallness is with respect to the chosen expansion variable and coefficients: in the clock example u=-v^2/c^2, so a quadratic term in u is fourth order in v/c. For a variable or very large r, |x| alone is not a uniform error guarantee.

findings.locator: PDF pp4-5 / printed pp3-4, time labels and GPS prose; Fig3
findings.source_claim: Identifies T as satellite time and Tprime as wristwatch time while invoking a pure special-relativistic time-dilation factor in a satellite setting.
findings.correction_or_qualification: Interpret T as satellite proper time and Tprime as the corresponding coordinate-time interval in an approximately inertial comparison frame; identify the same events and neglect gravity/orbital complications in this example. Real GPS requires additional gravitational and coordinate corrections.
findings.checked_deduction: For a constant-speed inertial segment, dT=dTprime sqrt(1-v^2/c^2) gives the printed exact ratio. Directly watching arriving ticks also involves signal propagation/Doppler effects. NIST Technical Note1385 section2.3 distinguishes coordinate time, motion-induced slowing and gravitational speeding, and describes the fixed GPS frequency offset. The source already acknowledges other approximations, so this is a model clarification, not a claim that it omits every GPS correction.

findings.locator: PDF p7 / printed p6, first paragraph
findings.source_claim: Says even the best atomic clocks cannot measure time at the approximately10^-20 level.
findings.correction_or_qualification: Treat this as a historical practical statement, and distinguish fractional correction, time error over a specified interval, frequency uncertainty and statistical precision; it is not a universal impossibility theorem.
findings.checked_deduction: For printedv=4 km/s andc=3e5 km/s, beta^2=1.7777778e-10 and the omitted3beta^4/8 term is1.1851852e-20 in the dimensionless factor. Absolute time error multiplies byT. A bounded NIST2025 primary abstract reports5.5e-19 systematic fractional-frequency uncertainty and explicitly time-dependent stability; it does not establish an exhaustive current world-best bound or a fundamental prohibition.
